sc7.changes.q: Ice melting: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Melting only changes state; it is still water.

sc7.changes.q: Water freezing: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Freezing only changes state; it is still water.

sc7.changes.q: Water boiling: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Steam is still water, only in gas form.

sc7.changes.q: Sugar dissolving: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: The sugar is still there; evaporate the water to get it.

sc7.changes.q: Salt dissolving: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: The salt is still there; evaporate the water to get it.

sc7.changes.q: Tearing paper: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Torn paper is still paper; no new substance forms.

sc7.changes.q: Breaking glass: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Broken glass is still glass; no new substance forms.

sc7.changes.q: Cutting vegetables: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Cut pieces are still the same vegetable.

sc7.changes.q: Stretching rubber band: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: A stretched band is still rubber and springs back.

sc7.changes.q: Melting wax: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Melted wax is still wax and hardens again.

sc7.changes.q: Chopping wood: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Chopped wood is still wood; only its size changes.

sc7.changes.q: Blowing up a balloon: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: The balloon only stretches; no new substance forms.

sc7.changes.q: Sharpening a pencil: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Shavings are still wood; no new substance forms.

sc7.changes.q: Grinding wheat to flour: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Flour is still wheat in tiny pieces.

sc7.changes.q: Melting butter: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Melted butter is still butter and sets again.

sc7.changes.q: Burning paper: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning makes ash, smoke and gases, which are new substances.

sc7.changes.q: Burning wood: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning wood makes ash and gases, which are new substances.

sc7.changes.q: Iron rusting: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Rust is a new substance made from iron, air and water.

sc7.changes.q: Boiling an egg: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Heat changes the egg's substances; it cannot become raw again.

sc7.changes.q: Milk turning to curd: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Curd is a new substance made from milk.

sc7.changes.q: Fruit ripening: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Ripening makes new substances that change taste and colour.

sc7.changes.q: Fruit rotting: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Rotting breaks fruit into new substances.

sc7.changes.q: Digesting food: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Digestion breaks food into new, simpler substances.

sc7.changes.q: Baking a cake: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Baking makes new substances; a cake cannot turn back to batter.

sc7.changes.q: Burning magnesium ribbon: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning magnesium makes a new white powder, magnesium oxide.

sc7.changes.q: Burning coal: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning coal makes new gases and ash.

sc7.changes.q: Vinegar with baking soda: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Vinegar and baking soda make carbon dioxide gas.

sc7.changes.q: Silver tarnishing: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: A dark new layer forms on silver.

sc7.changes.q: Copper turning green: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: A green new coating forms on copper in moist air.

sc7.changes.q: Lighting a firecracker: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning makes light, sound, smoke and new substances.

sc7.changes.q: Burning a matchstick: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning makes ash and gases, which are new substances.

sc7.changes.q: Petrol burning in a car: which kind of change is it?
sc7.changes.why: Burning petrol makes new gases.

sc7.changes.q: Photosynthesis in leaves: which kind of change is it?

sc7.plantLife.s: A destarched plant with green-and-white leaves is in sunlight in normal air. Iodine turns a green part of its leaf blue-black.
sc7.plantLife.why: Light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll were all there, so starch formed.

sc7.plantLife.s: A destarched plant with green-and-white leaves is in sunlight in normal air. Iodine turns a white part of its leaf blue-black.
sc7.plantLife.why: The white part has no chlorophyll, so no starch forms.

sc7.plantLife.s: A destarched plant with green-and-white leaves is in sunlight with carbon dioxide removed. Iodine turns a green part of its leaf blue-black.
sc7.plantLife.why: Without carbon dioxide, the leaf cannot make food.
